title: Saint Barnabas, Apostle
short_summary: Saint Barnabas was a Levite from Cyprus, an early disciple, and a trusted apostolic missionary whose work helped strengthen the Church at Antioch and the mission to the Gentiles.
key_facts: The Acts of the Apostles identifies Barnabas as a Levite from Cyprus.
His name is interpreted in Acts as son of encouragement.
He introduced Saul to the apostles after Saul's conversion.
He served the Church at Antioch and joined Paul in missionary work.
The U.S. calendar keeps him as a memorial on June 11.

sections.heading: An early apostolic witness
sections.body: Barnabas appears in Acts as a generous and trusted member of the early Church. He sold property for the good of the community and later helped bring Saul, the future Paul, into contact with the apostles when others still feared him.

sections.heading: Sent from Antioch
sections.body: Barnabas was connected closely with the Church at Antioch, where disciples of Jesus were first called Christians. Acts presents him and Paul being set apart for missionary work, and Barnabas shares in the apostolic mission to proclaim Christ beyond Jerusalem.

sections.heading: A man of encouragement
sections.body: His name is associated with encouragement, and his life shows that apostolic work includes strengthening others, recognizing grace in them, and serving the unity of the Church.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Apostolic mission
catholic_connection_sections.body: Barnabas reminds Catholics that the Church is missionary from her beginning. The Gospel is handed on through witnesses sent in communion with the apostolic Church.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Communion and trust
catholic_connection_sections.body: His support of Paul shows a Church that discerns, receives, and sends. Apostolic authority and missionary courage belong together.

historical_cautions: Barnabas is honored liturgically as an Apostle, but he is not one of the Twelve. This profile uses apostolic in the broader biblical and liturgical sense.
